{{short description|French mathematician (1826-1904)}}
{{about|the French mathematician|the American real estate man|Theophile Papin}}
'''Jean François Théophile Pépin''' (14 May 1826 – 3 April 1904) was a French mathematician.

Born in [[Cluses]], [[Haute-Savoie]], he became a [[Jesuit]] in 1846, and from 1850 to 1856 and from 1862 to 1871 he was Professor of Mathematics at various Jesuit colleges. He was appointed Professor of [[Canon Law]] in 1873, moving to [[Rome]] in 1880. He died in [[Lyon]] at the age of 77.

His work centred on [[number theory]]. In 1876 he found a new proof of [[Fermat's Last Theorem]] for ''n''&nbsp;=&nbsp;7,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Pepin T|author-link=Théophile Pépin|year=1876|title=Impossibilité de l'équation ''x''<sup>7</sup> + ''y''<sup>7</sup> + ''z''<sup>7</sup> = 0|journal=C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris|volume=82|pages=676–679, 743–747}}</ref> and in 1880 he published the first general solution<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Pepin T|author-link=Théophile Pépin|year=1880|title=Solution d'un Problème de Frenicle Sur Deux Triangles Rectangles|url=https://archive.org/details/attidellaaccade14lincgoog/|journal=Atti Accad. Pont. Nuovi Lincei|volume=33|pages=284–289}}</ref> to [[Frénicle de Bessy]]'s problem

:''x''<sup>2</sup> + ''y''<sup>2</sup> = ''z''<sup>2</sup>,&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;''x''<sup>2</sup> = ''u''<sup>2</sup> + ''v''<sup>2</sup>,&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;''x'' − ''y'' = ''u'' − ''v''.

He also gave his name to [[Pépin's test]], a test of primality for [[Fermat number]]s.
